title: Time and Work: Pipes and Cisterns (Level 1)

questions.q_en: Pipe P and Q together can fill a tank in 12 days. If pipe R can fill the same tank in 20 days, then in how much time P, Q and R together can fill the same tank?
questions.solution_en:
Total capacity = LCM of 12 and 20 = 60 units

Part filled by P and Q together = 60/12 = 5 units/day

Part filled by R = 60/20 = 3 units/day

Time taken by P, Q and R together = 60/(5+3) = 7.5 days
questions.solution_hi:

Part filled by P and Q together = 60/12 = 5 units/day

Part filled by R = 60/20 = 3 units/day

Time taken by P, Q and R together = 60/(5+3) = 7.5 days

questions.q_en: Pipe K can fill a cistern in 45 minutes and pipe L can empty the cistern in 30 minutes. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, What is the time taken by pipe K and L together to empty the cistern?
questions.solution_en:
The time taken by pipe K and L together to empty the cistern = 1/(1/45 - 1/30)

= (3-2)/90 minutes = 1/90 minutes

The time taken by pipe K and L together to empty the cistern is 90 minutes.

questions.q_en: Pipe A, pipe B and pipe C are three pipes that can fill a tank together in 12 hours and pipe C alone fill the same tank in 48 hours. Find the time taken by pipe A and pipe B together to fill the same tank.
questions.solution_en:
The capacity of tank = L.C.M of 12 and 48 = 48

The efficiency of pipe A, pipe B and pipe C = capacity of tank/ time taken = 48/12 =4

The efficiency of pipe C together = 48/ 48 = 1

The efficiency of pipe A and pipe B together = 4 - 1 = 3

Time = total capacity/ efficiency of pipe A and pipe B together

The time taken by pipe A and pipe B together to fill the same tank = 48/3

= 16 hours

questions.q_en: Three pipes are attached to a tank, pipe P and Q can fill a tank in 10 hours and 12 hours respectively while pipe R can empty the tank in 60 hours. If all the three pipes are opened together then find the total time it will take to fill the tank.
questions.solution_en:
Let the capacity of the tank = 60 units (LCM of 10, 12 and 60)

Efficiency of pipe P to fill the tank = 60/10 = 6 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe Q to fill the tank = 60/12 = 5 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe R to empty the tank = 60/60 = 1 unit/hour

Required time = 60/(6 + 5 - 1) = 60/10 = 6 hours

questions.q_en: Tap A can fill a tank in 20 hours and another tap B can empty two-fifth of the tank in 6 hours. Both the taps are opened together for 20 hours, then in how many hours the remaining tank can be emptied by Tap B alone if tank was completely filled initially?
questions.solution_en:
A = 20 hours

B = (5*6)/2 = 15 hours

Total capacity of tank = LCM of 20 and 15 = 60 units

Efficiency of Tap A = 60/20 = 3 units/hour

Efficiency of Tap B = 60/15 = - 4 units/hour (discharge tap)

Efficiency of A and B together = 3 - 4 = - 1 unit/hour

Tank emptied in 20 hours by A and B together = 20*1 = 20 units

Units left = 60 - 20 = 40

40 units get emptied by tap B alone

Units left/efficiency of B = 40/4 = 10 hours

questions.q_en: Two inlet pipes A and B and one outlet pipe C are attached to a tank and pipes A and B alone can fill the tank in 30 minutes and 42 minutes, respectively while pipe C alone can empty it in 18 minutes. If all the three are kept open simultaneously, when will the tank be full?
questions.solution_en:
Time is taken by A to fill the tank = 30 minutes

Time is taken by B to fill the tank = 42 minutes

Time is taken by C to empty the tank = 18 minutes

If all the three are kept open simultaneously,

Then tank will be filled in = 1/(1/30 + 1/42 - 1/18) = 630 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 160 minutes, 320 minutes and 400 minutes respectively. If all three pipes are opened together, then 19/20th part of tank will be filled in how much time (in hours)?
questions.solution_en:
Pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 160 minutes, 320 minutes and 400 minutes, respectively.

Total time in which the tank can be filled if all three are opened together = 1/(1/160 + 1/320 + 1/400) = 1600/19 minutes

Thus, time in which 19/20th part of tank will be filled = 19/20 * 1600/19 = 80 minutes = 80/60 hours = 4/3 hour

questions.q_en: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 25 minutes and 20 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened together and A is closed after 5 minutes then how many minutes will B take to fill the remaining tank?
questions.solution_en:
Part filled by pipe A in 1 minute = 1/25

Part filled by pipe B in 1 minute = 1/20

Part filled by pipe A and B together in 1 minute = 1/25 + 1/20 = 9/100

Part filled by pipe A and B together in 5 minutes = 45/100

Remaining part = 1 - 45/100 = 55/100

Therefore, time taken by pipe B to fill the remaining part of tank = 20 x (55/100) = 11 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe A can fill the tank in 8 hours. Pipe A is opened for 4 hours and after that pipe B is also opened but only for 2 hours and the tank is filled completely in a total of 13(1/3) hours. Which of the following statement is true for pipe B?
options_en: Pipe B can empty the tank in 3 hours.
Pipe B can fill the tank in 6 hours.
Pipe B can empty the tank in 2 hours.
Pipe B can fill the tank in 3 hours.
questions.solution_en:
Let pipe B can fill the tank in x hours.

According to the question,

4/8 + 2(1/8 + 1/x) + (40/3 - 6)/8 = 1

=> x = -3

Hence, pipe B can empty the tank in 3 hours.

questions.q_en: Two pipes P and Q together can fill a tank in 6 hours. If pipe P opened for first 4 hours, then the remaining part of the tank is filled by pipe Q alone in 9 hours. In how many hours Q can fill the tank alone?
questions.solution_en:
Let the efficiency of pipes P and Q be p and q respectively

(p + q) * 6 = 4p + 9q

6p + 6q = 4p + 9q

2p = 3q

p/q = 3/2

Total capacity of the tank = (3 + 2) * 6 = 30 units

Hence, Q will take = 30/2 = 15 hours to fill the tank.

questions.q_en: Pipe M can fill a cistern in (81/2) minutes. There is a leakage at the bottom of the cistern, due to which it takes (189/4) minutes for the cistern to be filled. How much time will the leakage take in emptying the cistern, if the cistern is completely filled initially?
questions.solution_en:
Pipe M can fill a cistern in = 81/2 minutes

And pipe M with leakage can fill the cistern in = 189/4 minutes

So, leakage alone can empty the tank in = 1/(2/81 - 4/189) = 567/2 minutes

questions.q_en: Two pipes P and Q can fill the tank in 15 minutes and 12 minutes respectively. If both the pipes are opened alternately for 1 minute, starting with P, then in how much time will the tank be filled completely?
questions.solution_en:
Part of the tank filled by pipe P in a minute = 1/15

Part of the tank filled by pipe Q in a minute = 1/12

Part fill by P and Q in 2 minutes = 1/15 + 1/12 = 9/60 = 3/20

Part filled in 12 minutes = 6*3/20 = 9/10

Remaining Part = 1 - 9/10 = 1/10

Part of the tank filled by pipe P in 1.5 minutes = 1.5*1/15 = 1/10

Hence, total time = 12 + 1.5 = 13.5 minutes

questions.q_en: Pipe A and pipe B can fill a tank in 25 hours and 50 hours respectively, then find the time it will take to fill 30% of the tank.
questions.solution_en:
Let the total capacity of tank = 50 units (LCM of 25 and 50)

Efficiency of the Pipe A = 50/25 = 2 units/hour

Efficiency of the Pipe B = 50/50 = 1 unit/hour

Required time = 3/10 * 50/(2 + 1) = 5 hours

questions.q_en: Two taps K and L can fill a tank in 40 hours and 60 hours respectively. Tap K opened first and after 10 hours tap L opened. How much time in total will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.solution_en:
Part of tank filled by tap K in 10 hours = 10/40 = 1/4

Remaining part to be filled = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4

Time taken by taps K and L together to fill 3/4th part of the tank

= 3/4 * 1/(1/40 + 1/60)

= 18 hours

Therefore, total time taken = 10 + 18 = 28 hours

questions.q_en: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 14 hours, 16 hours and 28 hours respectively. If pipe A and B together are opened for 3 hours, then in how much time will pipe C fill the remaining portion of the tank?
questions.solution_en:
A = 14 hours

B = 16 hours

C = 28 hours

Part of tank filled by pipe A and B together = 3 * ((1/14) + (1/16)) = 45/112

Remaining part = 1 - 45/112 = 67/112

Then, time taken by pipe C to fill the remaining part = (67/112) * 28 = 16.75 hours

questions.q_en: Pipe P, Q and R can fill a tank in 15 minutes, 20 minutes and 40 minutes respectively. What is the time taken to fill the tank when all three pipes are opened together?
questions.solution_en:
Capacity of tank = LCM of 15, 20 and 40 = 120 unit

Efficiency of pipe P = 120/15 = 8 unit

Efficiency of pipe Q = 120/20 = 6 unit

Efficiency of pipe R = 120/40 = 3 unit

Time taken to fill tank when all pipes are opened together = 120/(8 + 6 + 3)

= 120/17 or 7 (1/17) minutes

questions.q_en: Three pipes A, B, and C can fill the tank in 8 hours. Pipes B and C together can fill the tank in 16 hours. Find the time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank.
questions.solution_en:
The capacity of the tank = L.C.M of 8 and 16 = 16

Efficiency = capacity of tank/ time taken

Efficiency of pipes A, B, and C = 16/8 = 2

Efficiency of pipes B and C = 16/16 = 1

Efficiency of pipe A = 2 - 1 = 1

Required time taken = 16/1 = 16 hours

questions.q_en: Pipe A and pipe B together can fill the tank in 16 hours. Pipe B and pipe C together can fill the tank in 32 hours. Pipe C and pipe A together can fill the tank in 48 hours. Find the time taken by pipes A, B, and C to fill the tank.
questions.solution_en:
The capacity of tank = L.C.M of 16, 32, and 48 = 96

Efficiency = total capacity/ time taken

Efficiency of pipes A and B = 96/16 = 6

Efficiency of pipes B and C = 96/32 = 3

Efficiency of pipes C and A = 96/48 = 2

Efficiency of pipes A, B, and C = (6 + 3 + 2)/2 = 11/2

The required time = 96/ (11/2) = 192/11 hours

questions.q_en: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 16 hours and 24 hours respectively. If both the pipes open for alternate hours starting with pipe A, then find the time taken to fill the tank.
questions.solution_en:
Total capacity (LCM of 16 and 24) = 48 units

Efficiency of pipe A = 48/16 = 3 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe B = 48/24 = 2 units/hour

Total time taken = 2*45/(2 + 3) + 3/3 = 19 hours
